# 2D: AI

## Guide
- [Enemy patrol and chase](./Enemy-Patrol-and-Chase.md)

## Common patterns
Waypoint patrols provide predictable movement; distance tests detect nearby targets; Physics2D raycasts can check line of sight. Add explicit states as behavior grows: Patrol, Chase, Attack, Return, and Stunned are common examples.

## Debugging
Draw the detection ray, show waypoint gizmos, validate layer masks, and ensure AI does not compete with another controller for the same Rigidbody2D. Distance-only detection sees through walls unless you test occlusion.

# 2D: Animation

## Guides
- [Sprite animation and Animator](./Sprite-Animation-and-Animator.md)
- [Sprite flipping and aiming](./Sprite-Flipping-and-Aiming.md)

## Workflow
Import the sheet as Sprite (2D and UI), slice sprites in Sprite Editor, and create animation clips. Use an Animator Controller when states/parameters/transitions are useful; direct sprite assignment may suffice for very simple animations.

## Animator checks
Animator references the correct controller, clips are present in states, transition conditions refer to existing parameters with matching types, looping clips have Loop Time enabled, and no two systems control the same Transform property.

## Sprite consistency
Keep Pixels Per Unit and pivots consistent between frames. Use SpriteRenderer sorting/layers independently of physics layers. Test flipping with child weapons/colliders so visuals and hitboxes remain aligned.

# 2D: Audio

## Guide
- [Audio setup and sound effects](./Audio-Setup-and-Sound-Effects.md)

## AudioSource basics
- AudioClip: imported audio asset.
- AudioSource: playback component.
- AudioListener: usually on the active camera; keep a single active listener.
- AudioMixer: groups sources and controls volume/effects centrally.

For positional 2D effects, Spatial Blend is normally 0. Disable Play On Awake for code-triggered effects. Use PlayOneShot for short overlapping sounds; use looping AudioSources for music/ambience as appropriate.

## Import and performance
Audio import settings trade memory, latency, and CPU use. Choose based on clip duration and target platform. Profile rather than selecting one setting for every sound.

## Troubleshooting
Check source/listener enabled states, assigned clips, source volume, mixer routing/mute, Spatial Blend, pause state, and platform audio settings.

# 2D: Cameras

## Guides
- [Camera follow and pixel-perfect setup](./Camera-Follow-and-Pixel-Perfect.md)
- [Camera bounds and level confinement](./Camera-Bounds.md)
- [Screen shake recipe](../Recipes/Screen-Shake.md)

## Orthographic projection
Orthographic Size is half of the visible vertical world span. Visible width depends on aspect ratio. Set a deliberate camera Z position and ensure the gameplay plane is in front of the camera.

## Follow and confinement
Use LateUpdate for many simple follow cameras, or a camera package such as Cinemachine for richer rigs. Bounds must account for the camera's half-width and half-height. Integrate smoothing and clamping so one does not undo the other.

## Pixel art
Keep PPU/reference resolution consistent and test actual target resolution. Fractional camera positions can create shimmer or uneven pixel movement.
